meta.triageRationale: Feature: >1 task across external-endpoints.ts + entity storage (new deleteEntitiesById) + the TS/Python recognizers; real design in GC orphan-detection + precision-guarded dataflow recall.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: S003 detector follow-ups: edges-stat, endpoint GC, dataflow recall

api.name: deleteEntitiesById
api.signature: deleteEntitiesById(_db: DbClient, ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void>

parameters.name: ids
parameters.purpose: String entity ids to delete (the orphaned externalEndpoint ids).

returns.meaning: NEW storage primitive in src/db/entities.ts. For each id: look up its u64, delete the entity row, its name_index entry, the id<->u64 maps, and cascade its incident out/in edges — mirroring the deleteEntitiesForFile cascade but keyed by explicit id (needed because externalEndpoint entities share file='' so deleteEntitiesForFile is too coarse). Missing ids are skipped.

preconditions: ids are current entity ids (stale ids are no-ops).
postconditions: Each named entity + its incident edges are gone; other entities untouched; idempotent (deleting an absent id is a no-op).

api.name: resolveExternalEndpoints
api.signature: resolveExternalEndpoints(opts: { db: DbClient; repo: string } & ResolveExternalEndpointsDeps): Promise<ResolveExternalEndpointsResult>

returns.meaning: Existing pass (src/indexer/external-endpoints.ts) — TWO internal changes: (1) `edges` is now the count of DISTINCT (fromEntity,targetEntityId) pairs among promotes (was promotes.length, which double-counted a caller reaching one identity via two raw exprs); (2) after promoteResolvedBatch, a GC step lists this repo's externalEndpoint entities, keeps those with >=1 incident CALLS_HTTP in-edge (inNeighbors), and deletes the rest via deleteEntitiesById. Result shape may gain an optional `gcDeleted` count. ac1/ac2/idempotency invariants preserved.

preconditions: Runs after promoteResolvedBatch has written the current edges.
postconditions: edges reflects distinct edges; no externalEndpoint node in the repo has zero incident CALLS_HTTP edges after the pass; re-running on identical sources leaves the node/edge set unchanged (GC is a no-op when nothing orphaned).

api.name: parse
api.signature: parse(filePath: string, source: string, repo: string, repoId: number): ParseResult

returns.meaning: TS + Python parsers — SIGNATURE UNCHANGED. Internal: each pre-scans the file for a per-file Set of receivers PROVEN to be HTTP clients (TS: a constructor/method param or class field with a `HttpClient` type annotation → `this.<name>`; a `const x = axios.create(...)` → `x`. Python: `x = requests.Session()` / `httpx.Client()` → `x`). A call `<receiver>.<verb>(url)` whose receiver is in the Set AND verb is an HTTP verb emits an unresolved CALLS_HTTP (via emitCallsHttp). Receivers NOT proven HTTP never match — no bare `.get()`. Additive: existing module-rooted matches (fetch/axios.get/requests.get) + all other emission unchanged.

preconditions: The recognizer already runs inside the existing call walk (walkForCalls / walkPythonForHttpCalls).
postconditions: A proven-HTTP-receiver verb call yields one CALLS_HTTP with the raw URL; a same-named method on an unproven receiver yields no CALLS_HTTP; a no-HTTP file is byte-identical to before.

errorCases.scenario: The GC step would delete an endpoint that actually still has a live caller (a false-orphan), because the GC ran before the current pass wrote the edge.
errorCases.detection: GC reads inNeighbors(endpointU64, CALLS_HTTP) and sees zero in-edges for an endpoint that the current pass just minted.
errorCases.response: Order GC strictly AFTER promoteResolvedBatch(promotes) so all current edges are written before the incident-edge check; only then does zero-in-edges genuinely mean orphaned. GC never runs on the in-flight promote set.
errorCases.userImpact: None when ordered correctly; a mis-order would drop a live endpoint (recall loss) — prevented by the ordering + a test that a still-called endpoint survives GC.

errorCases.scenario: deleteEntitiesById is asked to delete an id that no longer exists (already gone / never existed).
errorCases.detection: The per-id u64 lookup returns undefined inside deleteEntitiesById.
errorCases.response: Skip that id (no-op) rather than throw — mirrors deleteEntitiesForFile's tolerance of already-cascaded rows; the batch continues.
errorCases.userImpact: None — GC is idempotent; a concurrent/duplicate delete is harmless.

errorCases.scenario: The dataflow pre-scan mis-identifies a receiver as an HTTP client (e.g. a local var named `http` not actually HttpClient-typed, or `x = requests.Session` without a call).
errorCases.detection: The pre-scan only adds a receiver when it sees a concrete proof node: a `HttpClient` type annotation on a param/field, or an RHS that is a CALL to axios.create / requests.Session / httpx.Client (not a bare reference).
errorCases.response: Require the proof node exactly (type-annotation identifier === 'HttpClient'; RHS is a call_expression whose callee text is the exact factory). A same-named-but-unproven receiver is never added to the set — no CALLS_HTTP. A precision-negative test pins this.
errorCases.userImpact: None — precision-over-recall: an unusual client construction is a recall gap, never a false positive.

edgeCases.input: One caller reaches ONE resolved identity via two distinct raw URL exprs (e.g. a literal and an interpolation both resolving to the same host).
edgeCases.expected: endpoints=1, edges=1 (distinct (from,to) pair) — not 2. The single LMDB edge already collapses; the stat now matches.

edgeCases.input: An endpoint that still has >=1 live CALLS_HTTP caller after re-index.
edgeCases.expected: GC keeps it (inNeighbors returns >=1); only zero-in-edge endpoints are deleted.

edgeCases.input: A repo re-indexed after ALL its HTTP calls were removed.
edgeCases.expected: Every externalEndpoint node becomes zero-in-edge and is GC'd; the repo ends with no endpoint nodes (no orphan cruft).

edgeCases.input: TS `this.http.get(url)` where `http` is a constructor param typed HttpClient; AND a local `foo.get()` where foo is unproven, in the same file.
edgeCases.expected: One CALLS_HTTP for this.http.get; none for foo.get.

edgeCases.input: Python `s = requests.Session(); s.get(url)` AND an unrelated `d.get('key')` on a dict.
edgeCases.expected: One CALLS_HTTP for s.get; none for d.get.

edgeCases.input: Re-running the endpoint pass on identical sources (nothing orphaned, no new edges).
edgeCases.expected: GC deletes nothing; node/edge set byte-identical; edges stat identical — idempotency preserved.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Zero false positives (S003 precision): HTTP recognition never emits CALLS_HTTP for a call on a receiver not statically proven to be an HTTP client — the dataflow set is built ONLY from concrete proof nodes (HttpClient type annotation / axios.create / requests.Session / httpx.Client calls).

Idempotent re-index (S003): re-running resolveExternalEndpoints on identical sources yields a byte-identical node/edge set — the GC only removes already-orphaned nodes (zero in-edges) and no-ops otherwise; deterministic ids for live endpoints are untouched.

Per-repo endpoint dedup + one-node-per-target (S003 ac1/ac2) is unchanged — the edges-stat fix only corrects the returned count; GC only deletes orphans; the recall change only ADDS emissions for proven receivers.

migration.stateBefore: S003 shipped: resolveExternalEndpoints (external-endpoints.ts) returns edges=promotes.length (over-counts distinct-rawExpr-same-identity); externalEndpoint nodes (file='') are never GC'd on re-index (deleteEntitiesForFile can't isolate them); the TS/Python recognizers match only module-rooted callees (fetch/axios.get/requests.get), missing instance-client calls (this.http.get, axios.create instances, requests.Session). Storage has only file/repo-scoped deletes, no per-id delete.
migration.stateAfter: edges = distinct (from,to) pair count; a post-pass GC deletes externalEndpoint nodes with zero incident CALLS_HTTP in-edges (via a new deleteEntitiesById primitive); the TS/Python recognizers ALSO match verb calls on receivers proven HTTP by intra-file dataflow (HttpClient DI / axios.create / requests.Session / httpx.Client), with zero false positives preserved. All changes land on re-index; no data rewrite.

migrationSteps.action: Add the new storage primitive deleteEntitiesById(db, ids) to db/entities.ts (additive export; no existing caller changes).

In resolveExternalEndpoints: compute edges as distinct (fromEntity,targetEntityId) pairs, and add the post-promote GC step (list repo externalEndpoint entities, keep those with >=1 CALLS_HTTP in-edge, deleteEntitiesById the rest). GC only removes already-orphaned nodes.
Extend the TS + Python recognizers with a per-file proven-HTTP-receiver pre-scan and receiver-in-set verb matching (additive emissions; module-rooted matching unchanged).
On the next repo re-index, orphaned endpoint nodes are swept and newly-recognized instance-client calls appear — no manual data migration; the graph converges on re-index.

migration.backwardCompat: No public signature changes: parse(), resolveExternalEndpoints(), and the LLMProvider surfaces are unchanged (deleteEntitiesById is purely additive; the endpoint pass may add an optional gcDeleted stat field). Existing graphs are compatible — the GC only removes nodes that are already orphaned; the recall change only ADDS edges/nodes for proven-HTTP calls; the edges-stat change affects a returned counter only, not stored data. Rolling back the code leaves any already-swept orphans gone (correct) and simply stops future GC/recall — no corruption.

alternativesConsidered.name: Proven-receiver dataflow set + deleteEntitiesById orphan GC + distinct-pair edges
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Item3: per-file Set of receivers PROVEN to be HTTP clients (HttpClient-typed param/field, axios.create/requests.Session/httpx.Client instances) drives verb-call matching; Item2: new deleteEntitiesById() deletes endpoints with zero incident CALLS_HTTP after the pass; Item1: edges = distinct (from,to) pairs.
pros: Precision preserved: only receivers statically proven to be HTTP clients match — keeps the S003 zero-false-positive stance (the crux).
GC is precise + minimal-churn: deletes exactly the orphaned endpoint ids, leaves live ones (and their deterministic ids/edges) untouched.
deleteEntitiesById is a reusable storage primitive (future kinds/GC can use it), filling a real gap (only file/repo-level deletes exist today).
edges stat becomes correct without touching the idempotent LMDB write.
cons: Most code: per-language dataflow pre-scan + a new storage helper + GC logic + tests across parsers, storage, and the endpoint pass.
Dataflow is intra-file only — a client passed across files/functions is still a recall gap (documented; precision-first).

alternativesConsidered.name: Import-gated verb matching (no receiver proof) + same GC/edges
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Item3 instead matches any `<recv>.<verb>(url)` when the file imports an HTTP lib (axios/@angular/common/http/requests/httpx), like the Java/Scala import gate — cheaper but looser.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest but violates precision-preserved — disqualifying under the accuracy-first principle. Reintroduces exactly what S003's fix removed (bare-verb matching misfires on unrelated .get()/.post() in an HTTP-importing file).
pros: Much less parser code — no per-file dataflow set; reuses the existing HTTP_LIBRARY_IMPORT_MARKERS gate pattern.
Catches more forms (any receiver) in HTTP-importing files.
cons: Re-introduces exactly the false-positive class S003 just fixed: a non-HTTP `.get()`/`.post()` on an unrelated object in a file that happens to import axios/requests would misfire — directly against the accuracy-first principle.
TS/JS were deliberately left UNgated in S003 (module-rooted receivers are unambiguous); import-gating + bare-verb matching is a precision regression for the language with the most such calls.

alternativesConsidered.name: Rebuild-from-scratch GC (delete all repo endpoints each pass) + a1 dataflow/edges
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Item2 instead deletes ALL of the repo's externalEndpoint nodes at the start of each pass and re-mints them, avoiding a new per-id helper; item3/1 as a1.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates idempotency (delete-all-then-remint churns ids/edges every index even when unchanged — breaks byte-identical re-index) + still needs a new bulk-delete primitive with worse churn and a mid-pass partial-delete failure window — strictly worse than a1's targeted GC.
pros: No new storage helper; GC is implicit (stale nodes never survive a pass).
cons: Churns deterministic ids/edges on EVERY index even when nothing changed — breaks the S003 idempotency invariant (byte-identical re-index) and wastes writes.
No repo-scoped externalEndpoint bulk delete exists either, so it ALSO needs a new storage primitive — no real saving over deleteEntitiesById, with worse churn.
A mid-pass failure could leave the repo with endpoints deleted and not yet re-minted.
